title: Conjecture on Planar Hat Guessing Number (Bosek et al. [4])
statement_text: The maximum possible hat guessing number of a planar graph is $4$.
context_text: Bosek, Dudek, Farnik, Grytczuk, and Mazur conjectured that $\mathrm{HG}(G) \leq 4$ for every planar graph $G$. This conjecture is the primary motivation for the paper's first main result.
attributed_to: Bosek, Dudek, Farnik, Grytczuk, and Mazur
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture by constructing a planar graph $G$ with $\mathrm{HG}(G) = 12$.
paper_title: On the Hat Guessing Number of Graphs

title: Conjecture on Hat Guessing Number vs. Hadwiger Number (Bosek et al. [4])
statement_text: The hat guessing number of any graph is at most its Hadwiger number, that is, the order of the largest clique minor of the graph.
context_text: Bosek et al. conjectured that $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ is bounded above by the Hadwiger number of $G$. The paper notes that the planar graph with $\mathrm{HG}(G)=12$ already provides a counterexample, and that for larger Hadwiger numbers $d$ the hat guessing number can in fact be at least doubly-exponential in $d$.
attributed_to: Bosek, Dudek, Farnik, Grytczuk, and Mazur
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture; the planar graph constructed has $\mathrm{HG}(G)=12$ while planar graphs exclude $K_5$ as a minor, giving Hadwiger number at most $4$.
paper_title: On the Hat Guessing Number of Graphs

title: Question on Degeneracy Bound for Hat Guessing Number (Alon et al. [1])
statement_text: Does there exist a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that if $G$ is $d$-degenerate, then $\mathrm{HG}(G) \leq f(d)$?
context_text: This question was raised in [1] (Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Shangguan, Tamo). A positive answer would imply that the hat guessing number of any planar graph is bounded by an absolute constant (since planar graphs are $5$-degenerate) and that $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ is bounded by a function of the Hadwiger number (since graphs with Hadwiger number $k$ are $O(k\sqrt{\log k})$-degenerate).
paper_contribution: The paper restates the question and notes that a positive answer seems plausible, but does not prove it.
paper_title: On the Hat Guessing Number of Graphs

title: Informal Belief on Degeneracy Bound for Hat Guessing Number
statement_text: It seems plausible that there exists a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $d$-degenerate graph $G$, $\mathrm{HG}(G) \leq f(d)$.
context_text: In the hat guessing game on a simple graph $G$, each vertex is a player who receives a hat of one of $q$ colours, chosen arbitrarily; each player sees only the hat colours of its neighbours, and after agreeing on a deterministic strategy, all players simultaneously guess their own colour, without communication. The players win if at least one guesses correctly. The hat guessing number $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ is the largest $q$ for which the players have a winning strategy. A graph is $d$-degenerate if every subgraph has a vertex of degree at most $d$. The question whether such an $f$ exists was raised by Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Shangguan and Tamo, and the authors find it plausible. It would imply that the hat guessing number of planar graphs (which are $5$-degenerate) is bounded by an absolute constant, and more generally that $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ is bounded by a function of the Hadwiger number (the order of the largest clique minor), since graphs with Hadwiger number $k$ are $O(k\sqrt{\log k})$-degenerate. It had been conjectured that planar graphs have hat guessing number at most $4$ and that $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ is at most the Hadwiger number; the authors refute both with a planar graph of hat guessing number $12$ (a later construction reaches $14$), and note that the hat guessing number can be doubly exponential in the Hadwiger number.
paper_title: On the Hat Guessing Number of Graphs

title: Question on Typical Hat Guessing Number of G(n,1/2)
statement_text: What is the typical asymptotic behavior of the hat guessing number of the random graph $G(n,1/2)$? In particular, is $\mathrm{HG}(G(n,1/2))$ equal to $o(n)$ with high probability?
context_text: In the hat guessing game on a simple graph $G$, each vertex is a player who receives a hat of one of $q$ colours, chosen arbitrarily; each player sees only the hat colours of its neighbours, and after agreeing on a deterministic strategy, all players simultaneously guess their own colour, without communication. The players win if at least one guesses correctly. The hat guessing number $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ is the largest $q$ for which the players have a winning strategy. $G(n,1/2)$ is the binomial random graph on $n$ vertices where each edge is present independently with probability $1/2$. It was known that with high probability $(2-o(1))\log_2 n\le\mathrm{HG}(G(n,1/2))\le n-(1+o(1))\log_2 n$; the authors improve the lower bound to $n^{1-o(1)}$ with high probability, leaving the true order of growth open.
paper_title: On the Hat Guessing Number of Graphs

title: Problem on Hat Guessing Number After Adding a Universal Vertex
statement_text: Establish an upper bound for $\mathrm{HG}(G')$ as a function of $\mathrm{HG}(G)$, where $G'$ is obtained from $G$ by adding a single vertex connected to all vertices of $G$, or show that no such function exists.
context_text: In the hat guessing game on a simple graph $G$, each vertex is a player who receives a hat of one of $q$ colours, chosen arbitrarily; each player sees only the hat colours of its neighbours, and after agreeing on a deterministic strategy, all players simultaneously guess their own colour, without communication. The players win if at least one guesses correctly. The hat guessing number $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ is the largest $q$ for which the players have a winning strategy. Let $G'$ be obtained from $G$ by adding one vertex adjacent to all vertices of $G$. Using graphs $G_d(N)$ of He and Li, each of which has a unique vertex adjacent to all others and whose removal leaves disjoint copies of $G_{d-1}(N)$, the authors observe that for arbitrarily large $q=\mathrm{HG}(G)$ one can have $\mathrm{HG}(G')=q^2+q$, so adding a universal vertex can increase the hat guessing number to more than $q^2$. The question is whether $\mathrm{HG}(G')$ is bounded by some function of $\mathrm{HG}(G)$.
paper_title: On the Hat Guessing Number of Graphs
